---
title: "Does ADS-C improve the OPDI results?"
subtitle: "One day run twice, without and with ADS-C position reports"
author: "EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit"
date: last-modified
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(knitr)

# Read-only. Every number and table on this page comes from a CSV file in
# data/, written by benchmarks/adsc_effect.py of the opdi repository. Nothing
# here reads S3, a database or a Spark cluster: data/_manifest.json records,
# for each file, the command, the git commit, a fingerprint of the source
# files and the tables it read.
D <- function(f, ...) read.csv(file.path("data", f), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, ...)
isT <- function(x) toupper(as.character(x)) == "TRUE"

ad   <- D("adsc_reports.csv")             # ADS-C reports and where they lie
tpf  <- D("tracks_per_flight.csv")        # reference flights by number of tracks, per run and flow
tpc  <- D("tracks_per_flight_changes.csv")
fg   <- D("flight_gaps.csv")              # time of the reference flights not covered by any report
gp   <- D("gaps.csv")                     # gaps inside tracks, by length
af   <- D("airports_found.csv")           # departure and destination airport against the reference
dst  <- D("distance.csv")                 # published distance flown against the reference route
ebt  <- D("events_by_type.csv")           # events matched between the two runs
fir  <- D("fir_crossings.csv")            # FIR crossings per FIR entered
eb   <- D("event_brackets.csv")           # time between the two reports around a crossing
fj   <- D("false_joins.csv")              # tracks holding two reference flights
pt   <- D("processing_time.csv", colClasses = c(step = "character"))

num <- function(x, d = 0) formatC(as.numeric(x), format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
pct <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(num(100 * x, d), "%")

A <- function(metric, col = "value") ad[ad$metric == metric, col]

# Totals over the four flows of the reference flights.
tot <- function(df, run, col) sum(df[df$run == run, col])
flights_ref <- tot(tpf, "base", "flights")
one_b <- tot(tpf, "base", "one_track");  one_m <- tot(tpf, "merged", "one_track")
unc_b <- tot(fg, "base", "uncovered_hours"); unc_m <- tot(fg, "merged", "uncovered_hours")
apt_b <- sum(af$base_both_right); apt_m <- sum(af$merged_both_right)
DI <- function(run, col) dst[dst$run == run & dst$population == "all", col]

# FIR crossings into oceanic FIRs, and crossings placed between two reports
# more than 300 s apart.
oce <- fir[isT(fir$oceanic), ]
B <- function(type, run, col) eb[eb$type == type & eb$run == run, col]

# New events inside the gaps of the run without ADS-C.
hole_new <- ebt[isT(ebt$in_base_hole), c("type", "only_merged")]
hole_new <- aggregate(only_merged ~ type, data = hole_new, FUN = sum)
hole_new <- hole_new[order(-hole_new$only_merged), ]
fir_new <- hole_new$only_merged[hole_new$type == "xing-fir"]

added <- function(step) pt$added_s[pt$step == step]
```

## Summary

ADS-C reports fill part of the long silences that ADS-B leaves over the oceans,
and on one day they made a few more long-haul flights come out as a single
track, with a distance flown closer to the reference. But the events they add
over the ocean have uncertain times, they create small separate pieces of
track, and they change the flight identifiers. ADS-C therefore stays switched
off in release v2.0.0; this note lists what would have to change first.

## What ADS-C is

OPDI is built from **ADS-B** reports, radio messages in which an aircraft
broadcasts its position, heard only by receivers within a few hundred
kilometres. **ADS-C** is a second source of position reports, sent by
satellite link, mainly over the oceans, at about one report every several
minutes per aircraft. The OpenSky Network publishes the ADS-C reports it
receives, and the pipeline can merge them into the ADS-B reports before it
builds tracks; this is switched off by default. An earlier study,
[ADS-C in the OPDI trajectory](../adsc-fusion-v1/index.qmd), described the
ADS-C data and the merge itself.

## How it was tested

- **One day**, 14 June 2026, worldwide.
- **The aircraft that sent ADS-C reports that day**:
  `r num(A("study_aircraft"))` aircraft. An aircraft without ADS-C gets the
  same tracks either way, so leaving it out changes nothing in the comparison.
- **The same pipeline run twice** on the same ADS-B reports, once without and
  once with the ADS-C reports. Nothing else differs between the two runs.
- **Reference flights**: the `r num(flights_ref)` flights of these aircraft
  that day recorded by EUROCONTROL's Network Manager, with their airports,
  times and route length. All of them touch Europe or its surroundings, so
  they are mostly flights to, from or within Europe.

A **gap** is a silence of more than 30 minutes between two reports of the same
aircraft. Inside a gap, no event is placed and a flight can be split into
several tracks.

## Where the ADS-C reports fall

Of the `r num(A("input_reports_on_day"))` ADS-C reports of the day,
`r num(A("kept_in_merged_tracks"))` ended up in tracks of the run with ADS-C.

```{r tbl-position}
#| echo: false
lab <- c(position_in_hole = "inside an ADS-B gap of more than 30 minutes",
         position_in_gap = "inside an ADS-B gap of 5 to 30 minutes",
         position_near_adsb = "less than 5 minutes from an ADS-B report",
         position_before_first_adsb = "before the first ADS-B report of the aircraft",
         position_after_last_adsb = "after the last ADS-B report of the aircraft",
         position_no_adsb = "aircraft with no ADS-B report")
p <- ad[ad$metric %in% names(lab), ]
kable(data.frame(where = lab[p$metric], n = num(p$value), share = pct(p$share)),
      row.names = FALSE, align = "lrr",
      col.names = c("Where the ADS-C report lies", "Reports", "Share"),
      caption = paste0("The ", num(A("kept_in_merged_tracks")),
                       " ADS-C reports kept in the tracks, by distance in time to the ADS-B reports."))
```

So `r pct(A("position_in_hole", "share"))` of the ADS-C reports lie where ADS-B
says nothing for more than half an hour: they bring new information. The gaps
inside tracks become shorter (@fig-gaps).

```{r fig-gaps}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Time inside reception gaps of the tracks, by length of the gap, without and with ADS-C, in hours. Long gaps are cut into shorter ones."
#| fig-height: 4
cls <- unique(gp$gap_class)
m <- rbind(without = gp$gap_hours[gp$run == "base"][match(cls, gp$gap_class[gp$run == "base"])],
           with = gp$gap_hours[gp$run == "merged"][match(cls, gp$gap_class[gp$run == "merged"])])
colnames(m) <- cls
par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
barplot(m, beside = TRUE, col = c("grey70", "steelblue"), border = NA,
        xlab = "Length of the gap", ylab = "Time in gaps (hours)", las = 1, cex.names = 0.8,
        legend.text = c("without ADS-C", "with ADS-C"),
        args.legend = list(x = "topleft", bty = "n"))
```

## Results

```{r tbl-results}
#| echo: false
res <- data.frame(
  what = c(paste0("Reference flights rebuilt as exactly one track (of ", num(flights_ref), ")"),
           "Time of the reference flights not covered by any report",
           paste0("Reference flights with both airports right (of ", num(flights_ref), ")"),
           paste0("Distance flown within 5% of the reference route length (",
                  num(DI("base", "flights")), " flights with uncovered time)"),
           "Crossings into oceanic FIRs",
           "FIR crossings placed between two reports more than 5 minutes apart",
           "Tracks holding two reference flights"),
  base = c(pct(one_b / flights_ref), paste(num(unc_b), "h"), num(apt_b),
           pct(DI("base", "share_within_5pct_of_reference")),
           num(sum(oce$crossings_base)), num(B("xing-fir", "base", "over_limit")),
           num(fj$false_joins[fj$run == "base"])),
  merged = c(pct(one_m / flights_ref), paste(num(unc_m), "h"), num(apt_m),
             pct(DI("merged", "share_within_5pct_of_reference")),
             num(sum(oce$crossings_merged)), num(B("xing-fir", "merged", "over_limit")),
             num(fj$false_joins[fj$run == "merged"]))
)
kable(res, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrr",
      col.names = c("", "Without ADS-C", "With ADS-C"),
      caption = "The two runs compared, 14 June 2026.")
```

### Tracks

With ADS-C, `r num(one_m)` of the `r num(flights_ref)` reference flights come
out as exactly one track, against `r num(one_b)` without. In detail,
`r num(sum(tpc$became_one_track))` flights became one track and
`r num(sum(tpc$stopped_being_one_track))` stopped being one. Of those
`r num(sum(tpc$stopped_being_one_track))`, `r num(sum(tpc$no_track_left_on_the_day))`
have no track left on the day: an ADS-C report before midnight joined them to
a track that starts the day before. The other
`r num(sum(tpc$stopped_being_one_track) - sum(tpc$no_track_left_on_the_day))`
became two tracks. Reading these flights during the run showed that 7 of them
gained a separate small piece made only of ADS-C reports, which has no call
sign, and 3 were real splits; this reading is not recorded in the committed
files.

No track holds two reference flights in either run, so the ADS-C reports did
not wrongly join two flights. The number of tracks of these aircraft went from
`r num(fj$tracks[fj$run == "base"])` to `r num(fj$tracks[fj$run == "merged"])`,
and `r num(fj$tracks_with_adsc[fj$run == "merged"])` tracks contain ADS-C
reports. The flight identifier (`flight_id`) depends on the aircraft and on
the reports that make up its track, so wherever ADS-C moves the start of a
track, joins two tracks or splits one, the identifier differs from the one
without ADS-C.

### Coverage, airports and distance

The time of the reference flights that no report covers fell from
`r num(unc_b)` h to `r num(unc_m)` h. Departure and destination airports
barely change: `r num(apt_m)` flights have both airports right with ADS-C,
against `r num(apt_b)` without, because ADS-C reports are almost all at cruise
height, far from airports.

The published distance flown is the sum of the distances between consecutive
reports, so a long gap shortens it. Over the `r num(DI("base", "flights"))`
reference flights with uncovered time, the share within 5% of the route length
recorded by the Network Manager rose from
`r pct(DI("base", "share_within_5pct_of_reference"))` to
`r pct(DI("merged", "share_within_5pct_of_reference"))`.

### Events

New events appear inside the former gaps:

```{r tbl-new-events}
#| echo: false
h <- hole_new[hole_new$only_merged >= 10, ]
other <- sum(hole_new$only_merged[hole_new$only_merged < 10])
tab <- data.frame(type = c(paste0("`", h$type, "`"), "other types"),
                  n = num(c(h$only_merged, other)))
kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "lr",
      col.names = c("Event type", "New events"),
      caption = "Events found only with ADS-C, inside a gap of the run without ADS-C.")
```

They are mostly the start and end of level segments, `r num(fir_new)` FIR
crossings (an **FIR**, flight information region, is a block of airspace under
one air traffic service) and tops of climb and descent. Crossings into oceanic
FIRs rose from `r num(sum(oce$crossings_base))` to
`r num(sum(oce$crossings_merged))`.

The times of these events are uncertain. A FIR crossing is placed on the first
report inside the new region, and its `info` records the time since the
report before it. With ADS-B, reports are about 5 s apart; with ADS-C they can
be many minutes apart, so the crossing can be many minutes late. The FIR
crossings placed between two reports more than 5 minutes apart rose from
`r num(B("xing-fir", "base", "over_limit"))`
(`r pct(B("xing-fir", "base", "over_limit_share"))` of all FIR crossings) to
`r num(B("xing-fir", "merged", "over_limit"))`
(`r pct(B("xing-fir", "merged", "over_limit_share"))`); one crossing in ten now
has at least `r num(B("xing-fir", "merged", "p90_bracket_s"))` s between its
two reports, against `r num(B("xing-fir", "base", "p90_bracket_s"))` s without
ADS-C.

### Processing time

Reading the ADS-C reports took `r num(pt$shared_inputs[pt$step == "01b"])` s.
The later steps took `r num(sum(pt$merged, na.rm = TRUE))` s with ADS-C and
`r num(sum(pt$base, na.rm = TRUE))` s without; step 04 was even
`r num(-added("04"), 1)` s faster with ADS-C, which is most likely the usual
variation between two runs. The extra time is small.

## Recommendation

ADS-C helps long oceanic flights a little: slightly more of them are one track,
less of their time is uncovered, and their distance flown is closer to the
reference. But:

- the events it adds over the ocean have uncertain times, up to many minutes;
- it creates small separate pieces of track made only of ADS-C reports,
  without a call sign;
- it changes the flight identifiers of the tracks whose start it moves, or
  that it joins or splits, so data with and without ADS-C cannot be joined on
  `flight_id`.

ADS-C reports are therefore **not used in release v2.0.0**. Before they could
be, the following would have to change:

1. An event placed between two reports far apart, such as a FIR crossing, gets
   an estimated time and a stated uncertainty, or is left out.
2. A piece of track made only of ADS-C reports is attached to the flight it
   belongs to, or dropped.
3. The change of flight identifiers is published as a new track rule, so users
   know that identifiers before and after it do not match.
4. The effect is measured again on several days and on all aircraft, not only
   those with ADS-C.

## Limits

- One day was measured.
- Only aircraft that sent ADS-C that day were run. The totals describe these
  aircraft, not the whole fleet.
- The reference flights all touch Europe or its surroundings; flights
  elsewhere, for example over the Pacific, are not checked against a
  reference.

## Provenance

Every number and table on this page is read from the CSV files in `data/` when
the page is rendered; nothing is computed on a cluster, and the page needs no
credentials. The files were written by `benchmarks/adsc_effect.py` of the opdi
repository. `data/_manifest.json` records, for each file, the command and its
arguments, the git commit, whether the working copy had uncommitted changes, a
fingerprint of the source files and the tables it read. In the files, `base`
is the run without ADS-C and `merged` the run with it.
